boundary.startingEvent: A pick of the 'color' row from doset_simple()'s menu, or of 'use_inverse' from the full 'mO' menu, which options.c optfn_boolean() answers by setting go.opt_need_redraw and go.opt_need_glyph_reset.
boundary.endingEvent: The screen the port draws after reset_needed_visuals() returns, with every remembered out-of-sight terrain square repainted under the option value now in force rather than the one in force when the square was recorded.
boundary.validInputs: A pick of 'color' or of 'use_inverse'; any level whose remembered squares include terrain, which is every level. The four wall sets are selected by u.uz through In_mines, In_hell, Is_knox and In_sokoban, so a session in any branch is inside the boundary.
boundary.observables: levl[x][y].glyph as a cmap glyph number in map memory rather than a resolved presentation; the colour every terrain cell prints, which C takes from defsyms[].color, wallcolors[] and altarcolors[] under iflags.use_color; the four MG_BW_* glyphflags and the attribute they produce at print time; and the screens and cursors of the repaint. No ported arm may consume randomness.
boundary.exclusions: reset_glyphmap()'s CMAP_C and ZAP arms, which sit above the nine cmap arms in the chain and reach no map memory. The monster ranges and the 'wizmgender' refusal, which a later slice owns. The rogue-level terms, which reglyph_darkroom() already refuses.

The colour tables: defsyms[].color, the last argument of every PCHAR and PCHAR2 row in include/defsym.h, read through the cmap_color macro at src/display.c:2684; wallcolors[] at :2677 through wall_color at :2693; altarcolors[] at :2666 through altar_color at :2694. All three macros are gated on iflags.use_color, which is where the 'color' option reaches every terrain cell.
candidateListMethod.reachableHelpers: The nine map-memory cmap arms of reset_glyphmap(), read in chain order: GLYPH_CMAP_B_OFF with its !iflags.use_color switch raising MG_BW_LAVA, MG_BW_ICE and MG_BW_SINK; GLYPH_ALTAR_OFF; GLYPH_CMAP_A_OFF with the S_litcorr recolour and the MG_BW_ENGR arm; then the four wall sets SOKO, KNOX, GEH and MINES; then MAIN; then STONE. The CMAP_C and ZAP arms sit above them and reach no map memory.
candidateListMethod.javascriptCrossCheck: At the slice base bb7d62f, `grep -c 'terrainCmap(' js/display.js` returns 61 and `grep -n 'remembered_glyph = |remembered_glyph_from_presentation(' js/display.js` returns fourteen writer sites, so the conversion touches far more of the file than the object slice did. js/detect.js also writes one through remembered_glyph_from_presentation().
candidateListMethod.remainingLimits: Two. The wall-set selection reads u.uz, so a session in a branch the development set does not visit exercises a wall set no differential covers; wallcolors[] is uniformly CLR_GRAY today, which hides the difference. And no development session picks 'color' or 'use_inverse', so the whole slice rests on fresh differentials rather than on the development score, whose only role here is to show that nothing regressed.

entries.evidence: The live macro is one contiguous range from GLYPH_CMAP_STONE_OFF to GLYPH_CMAP_C_OFF + ((S_goodpos - S_digbeam) + 1). GLYPH_ZAP_OFF sits inside that span, since the enum order at 522-524 is CMAP_B, then ZAP, then CMAP_C, so the macro answers true for a zap glyph. The precise decomposition directly above it at 711-722, which excludes the zap range, is disabled under `#if 0` with the comment that it 'expands to a lot of unnecessary code'. glyphs.c:983 writes `glyph_is_cmap(glyph) || glyph_is_cmap_zap(glyph)`, a disjunction that is redundant under the live macro and meaningful under the disabled one.
entries.remaining: Transcribe the live contiguous form under AGENTS.md's rule to preserve behavior that looks accidental, and say in a comment that the block above it is not what the program compiles. Keep it distinct from js/display.js map_glyphinfo()'s own gate, which is a port-local assertion and must stay narrower, since a zap or CMAP_C number would reach a chain with no arm for it.

sourceReview: Traced by the orchestrator at bb7d62f, the slice base, against the C source and against the JavaScript as it stood before the worker's change. Read in full: src/display.c back_to_glyph() and the nine map-memory cmap arms of reset_glyphmap() with their three colour macros and two colour tables; include/display.h's cmap glyph macros and both definitions of glyph_is_cmap, the live one and the disabled precise one; and the enum order that puts GLYPH_ZAP_OFF inside the live macro's span. The trace covered state and random-number order: no arm in scope consumes randomness, and the wall arms' branch dependence through u.uz is state read at record time rather than at repaint time. Not yet traced: display.c map_glyphinfo()'s cmap half beyond the arms named here, and the twelve C call sites of glyph_is_cmap() beyond confirming that they exist and that one of them pairs it with glyph_is_cmap_zap(). Those gaps are the two entries carrying status undecided and the limits recorded in remainingLimits.
